Acquire · the KYC wall · EU account, October 202602 / 12

"Make your move into bitcoin," it said. Then it asked for my ID and financial information.

The fix: a web guest home (E0), tested 80/20 on strike.me. Value first, email only, the ID check when money moves. Kraken, Bitpanda and Trade Republic let you look around first (slide 03). Prototype ↗ · Tap a screen to see what it asks for.

Now

Proposed

Acquire · how Europe does it · 17 apps checked03 / 12

Kraken, Bitpanda and Trade Republic let you look around first. Strike asks for ID before you see anything.

Look around first, show ID when you add money
KrakenOpens on the home screen. ID only when you deposit or buy
BitpandaYour account comes first. ID when you add money
Trade RepublicYou can look around. No deposits until you’ve shown ID
BitstackThe app opens, with some features locked until you’re approved
RelaiOpens on the home screen. ID before your first buy

eToro goes further: every account gets a $100,000 practice portfolio, and you can deposit up to $2,250 before its checks finish.

ID first, before you see a single number
StrikeID and money questions before you see a single price
RevolutN26Crypto.comBitvavo21bitcoinRobinhoodScalable

No app lets you buy bitcoin before showing ID any more. Relai stopped in November 2024, Pocket in December 2025.

Is this allowed?Yes, as long as no money moves. Malta’s anti-money-laundering regulator, which supervises Strike in Europe, says checks start when someone “takes active steps to benefit from a service”. Asking for ID before that would be “premature”.

From each app’s help pages and terms, read 13 Nov 2026, and Malta’s anti-money-laundering rules (FIAU, Part I, section 4.6.1). Buying, holding and withdrawing still need ID first, and loans stay off the page. The rules in full: appendix A4. All 17 apps, and how money gets in: appendix A5. Invity: appendix A6.

Acquire · the cheap test · web first, app at the gatePrototype ↗04 / 12

Strike could also show value before it asks for anything. A cheap test: a web prototype, routed from strike.me.

  1. Webstrike.mefullGet started, not sign up. Sure.
  2. WebHomecuriousAdd money, prices in euros. No ID yet. Fine.
  3. WebAdd money+3€500, half buys bitcoin as it lands. Now I get it.
  4. WebSave−1Just an email to keep this? Fine.
  5. Web → AppDownload−2My settings come with me? OK, I'll install it.
  6. AppVerify−5ID, because I'm about to move money. Fair.
  7. AppPayaha€500 and auto-buy, still set. Pay.

The test: “Sign up” on strike.me, split to this web home. Read: funded within 7 days, per install; about 10 weeks at 50 / 50, 16 at 80 / 20. No lift, it’s off. Web only, nothing personal asked, no loans before the ID check. The split and the kill rule: appendix A2. The rules: appendix A4.

Pull: the habit lives in StrikeThe user changes, pauses or stops it in the app, and Strike collects on its own schedule. It needs a hold or a refund policy for eight weeks.

Retain · why a card · the evidence, Europe first09 / 12

Where people spend, they stay. A card keeps people, and rarely makes money.

They move in · Revolut+45%more customers made Revolut their primary bank in 2025, while all users grew 30%. Card payments bring 22% of its revenueRevolut · annual report 2025
They stay · UK banks3%of UK current-account customers switch bank in a year. Over half have kept their main account for 10+ yearsUK CMA · 2016
They stay · Robinhood, US~95%of Robinhood Gold Card customers stayed after their first transaction. No European app publishes a number like itRobinhood · Q3 2024 call
They bring friends · Monzo79%of Monzo’s customers joined through word of mouth. Its product chief has called the coral card a big part of its growthMonzo · annual report 2026
They queue for it · Revolut430kjoined the waitlist for Revolut Ultra, a £540-a-year platinum card. Bitstack’s bitcoin card went first to 5,000 waitlisters, in JanuaryRetail Banker Int’l 2023 · Bitstack 2026
It rarely pays · EU law0.2%the most a European debit card earns on a purchase, capped since 2015. Small US banks earn about 1.4%EU Regulation 2015/751

No European app publishes retention for cardholders against everyone else; the nearest proof is the primary bank. Each number compares people who chose with people who didn’t. The one study that controls for that (Management Science, 2010) still finds frequent users stay longer, while short-term profit falls.

Revolut annual report 2025, pages 9, 13 and 23; Monzo annual report 2026; TechCrunch, July 2020; UK Competition and Markets Authority, retail banking report, 2016; Retail Banker International, June 2023; Bitstack, December 2025; Robinhood earnings call, Q3 2024; EU Regulation 2015/751; Federal Reserve interchange data, 2024; Campbell and Frei, Management Science 2010. The US numbers, from Block, Coinbase and Gemini: appendix A15.

Appendix A21
Why the order mattersEvery visit can add a deposit, every deposit grows the stack, and a bigger stack is a bigger possible loan. Every stacker may be a borrower in waiting; lose people early and there is no one left to lend to.Two markets, two jobs. In the US, turn stackers into borrowers. In the EU, keep the people who sign up and grow their stacks: Strike lends there from €5,000, in some countries.

Appendix · acquire · the experiment in full: funnel model, scenarios and kill ruleAppendix · A2

Split “Sign up” 80 / 20. Would experiencing value before KYC lift the funding rate?

80% · control · today
Download app→Sign up→Email→KYC→Home · $0→Fund
20% · variant · web guest home
Home · tiles→Add money or calculator→Email→Download app→KYC · numbers waiting→Fund
HypothesisIf people see their own numbers before any ID ask, a loan in the US and a first deposit in sats in the EU, more of them fund within 7 days.
ScopeWeb only. At a typical baseline, about 3 in 100 clicks funded, a 25% lift takes about 16 weeks to read at 80/20 and 10 at 50/50. 80/20 protects sign-ups, 50/50 learns faster: your call. The app and KYC don’t change.
ReadPrimary: funded within 7 days, per install. Not per sign-up: moving the ID check later lowers “verified per sign-up” even when it works. No lift by then, it’s off.
Open the funnel model ↗

Cheap, reversible and web only: a learning vehicle. The payoff is the same change inside the app: $0.1M–$0.9M first-year revenue if funding rises a quarter to double, on about 12,000 installs a month and $60–120 a funded user.

Research, 13 Nov 2026: 3 in 100 clicks funded is typical (the model said 9.4%); installs look nearer 12,000 a month than 50,000; $150 a funded user is high, and too high at EU fees. Strike’s own installs and funded rate settle it. No loans on the web in the EU or UK. Others that let people in first: slide 03.

Appendix · activate · EU · the first depositAppendix · A3

Funding today is a copied IBAN. Make auto-buy the reason to deposit.

TodayAuto-buy is a small toggle above the IBAN, off, with one line of copy. It doesn't say what it buys, how much, or why you'd want it.
ProposedPick how to pay. Auto-buy moves to the top, on by default, with a share slider, a live "what you get" and three steps. Try the toggle, the share and the amount. Illustrative price: €68,000 per bitcoin.
Apple Pay12 of 17 apps take cards. Costs at least €0.32–0.42 per €100 before the acquirer’s margin and fraud; disputes run 120 days; 3–6 months to add. A question for you.
MetricFunded within 7 days, and auto-buy on at 30 days. Pay by bank: about €1.20 per €100 at the one vendor that publishes a price, no chargebacks, 1–3 months. Instant transfers are free at euro banks since Oct 2025.

Appendix · acquire · what moved onboarding numbers elsewhereAppendix · A7

Cutting friction at sign-up moves numbers. Nobody has published what showing value first does.

Monzo US · 20249% → 19%of installs became open accounts after sign-up was cut from 39 screens to 17; 40% once low-risk users could skip one check. Median time: 17 minutes to 7Monzo · company blog, Sep 2024
Wise · SwedenUnder 5 minfor everyone who verified with their bank’s eID, against 40% of those with a photo of their ID; 8% fewer gave up, 9% more passed, at 42× lower costWise · 2021 · people chose their method
Wise · Australia26% → 40%of Android sign-ups onboarded instantly once background data checks replaced document stepsWise · 2019
Robinhood13 → <5 monthsto earn back acquisition cost after the referral reward moved from approval to bank linking, alongside ad changesRobinhood · 2021 IPO filing
Coinbase~90%of people who submit an ID pass, once automated checks cut verification from hours to secondsCoinbase · 2018
Showing value firstNonepublished. Coinbase, Bitstack, Fold and Kraken let people look first, but no one has shared the effect. Strike’s test would be the firstExperiments research, Nov 2026

Vendors’ own claims, for scale: Plaid says Gemini’s first deposits got 8× faster; TrueLayer says drop-off before a first deposit fell from 57% to 20%; Onfido says 80% of bunq users are approved in seconds.

Monzo’s US blog (Sep 2024); Wise’s blog and engineering posts (2019, 2021); Robinhood’s S-1 (2021); Coinbase’s blog (2018). Read the test per install, not per sign-up: moving the ID check later lowers “verified per sign-up” even when it works.

Activated could mean funded, with auto-buy on. Three numbers may show whether the first deposit works.

Metric 1Verified to fundedShare of verified users who deposit within 7 days. This is where a SEPA-only, copy-the-IBAN step may lose people.
Metric 2Time to first satsHours from opening the deposit screen to owning bitcoin. Today it takes a bank transfer, then a separate buy.
Metric 3Auto-buy on at day 30Share of funded users with any auto-buy on. It is the earliest sign that a habit has started.
The experiment
TestAuto-buy prompt at the first deposit, on by default, with a share slider (appendix A3). Half of new EU depositors see it, half see today's screen.
ReadMetric 3 first, then whether those users are still funding at day 60.
Kill ruleNo lift in auto-buy at day 30 after four weeks, or more people turning it off than keeping it.
AskApple Pay and Google Pay, two ways. Charge the user what it costs, as Bitstack (0.70%), Relai (3%) and Kraken (3.75% + €0.25) do. Or carry €0.62 to €3.12 per €100 for a faster first deposit. A question for you, not a test (appendix A17 and the model).

My proposal, not Strike data. Baselines for all three metrics are in appendix A23.

Competitors · how Invity makes moneyAppendix · A13

Invity monetises the stacker three ways. Strike EU's recurring buys are free.

1 · Every buyA service fee on each purchaseShown before you confirm, 1.49% on one Invity page. No monthly subscription. Friends get 10% off fees for life, and the referrer earns 33% of that fee.invity.io fees and referral pages
2 · Extra buying powerTurbo Buy: +60% at 9.9% a yearThe extra 60% on each recurring buy is charged 9.9% a year, on the extra only. Invity says 89% of customers were in profit after a year and none was liquidated. Those are its claims.invity.io Turbo Buy
3 · Cash against the stackLoans as a fixed buybackUp to 50% of value, 1 to 36 months, a fixed buyback price and "no debt". Business loans are 50% LTV, non-recourse, from €4,000. Cash Out is still coming soon in the app.invity.io loans · Invity iOS app, 9 Nov
The card is a retention loop, not the revenueCashback is 1.5% for applicants by 30 Nov, then 1%, capped by your monthly auto-buy and starting at €240 a month. EU interchange is capped at 0.2%, so my reading is that it rebates fee income earned on the stack.
What Strike can borrowRewards gated by auto-buy, not a subscription. A buyback-structured cash-out. Both are questions for you, not builds.

Appendix · why a card · the US evidenceAppendix · A15

In the US, where people spend, they stay. A card keeps people, and rarely makes money.

They stay≈10×gross profit per user from Cash App customers who spend $500+ a month or get paid into it, against those who only send moneyBlock · Q4 2025 letter
They stay~95%of Robinhood Gold Card customers stayed after their first transaction, with higher depositsRobinhood · Q3 2024 call
They use it$3,000spent a month per Coinbase One cardholder. Coinbase One members keep 4.2× the balancesCoinbase · 2025–2026
They show it48%of platinum cardholders gave up cash back on other cards to use the one others could seeQuarterly Journal of Economics · 2018
They queue for it~2Mjoined the waitlist for Robinhood’s metal Gold Card in seven monthsRobinhood · 2024
It rarely pays−$8.6MGemini’s card in Q2 2026: $16.2M of revenue, less $8.7M of rewards and $16.1M set aside for lossesGemini · Q2 2026 release

Each number compares people who chose the card with people who didn’t. The one study that controls for that, on online banking (Management Science, 2010), finds the same: frequent users stay longer, and short-term profit falls.

Block shareholder letter, Q4 2025; Robinhood earnings call, Q3 2024; Coinbase shareholder letter, Q4 2025, and earnings deck, Q3 2026; Bursztyn and others, QJE 2018; Gemini earnings release, Q2 2026 (before running costs); Campbell and Frei, Management Science 2010. Crypto.com shows the risk: it tied card tiers to staking its token, and users threatened to leave when it cut rewards in 2022. Europe’s numbers: slide 09.

Appendix · retain · the Travel Rule experimentAppendix · A19

Remember who people pay, prefill what the invoice already says. If paying gets easier, people may come back more often.

The experiment
BetMost EU spending is repeat: the same café, the same biller. Two steps instead of six for a known recipient could turn Strike into something you open every week.
TestRemember recipients and providers, prefill name and amount from the invoice. Half of EU users who have paid by Lightning at least once get it.
ReadSpend events per active user per month, then month-3 retention for the same group.
Kill ruleNo lift in spend events after eight weeks, or no change in month-3 retention after a quarter.
Why it mattersFrequency feeds the stackEach visit is a chance to deposit or buy. More visits tend to mean a bigger stack, and a bigger stack is the collateral for a loan (appendix A21).
US versionBill Pay already does thisPayday and bills bring US users back without a test. The question is how often, and how long they stay (A23).
ScopeNo card, no new licenceTravel Rule data is stored once and reused, not asked again. Whether that holds for every provider is a check for your compliance team.

My proposal, not Strike data. The six steps are from my own EU account (slide 08). Row 2 of the backlog (appendix A22).

Appendix · borrow · US · sized to the stackAppendix · A21

Show the borrow number sized to the stack the person already built.

TriggerAfter N months of stacking, not at sign-up. “You've stacked 0.31 ₿ over 7 months. At 50% LTV that's $X available without selling.” N: Strike’s data (A23, question 5).
Why it worksThe number is the user's, so it reads as information, not a sales pitch. Selling to pay a bill is the alternative; the calculator shows the tax you'd owe on that sale next to the interest.
MetricBorrowers with a first draw within 30 days of the prompt, by months stacked. Guard: credit disclosures already in the US flow.
An optional question, not an askStrike's no-liquidation loan is capped at 50% LTV with a six-month term. Would a small, capped, volatility-proof Boost on recurring buys suit stackers of six months or more? Reg Z disclosures; a quarter or more. Only if Strike wants it.

Verdicts: the stack-sized calculator is a test behind a flag, no licence change. The Boost is a question for Strike, not a recommendation. In the EU, Strike lends from €5,000 in some countries, at 10.50% APR and up. Precedent: Invity shows a loan explainer and calculator before ID (appendix A6).

Appendix · the questions only Strike can answerAppendix · A23

Eleven numbers only Strike has, and six calls only you can make.

1How much “Sign up” traffic is mobile web?→ where E0 runs first
2What share of verified accounts fund within 7 days?→ the baseline the test must beat
3What share of funded users have any auto-buy on at 30 days?→ the size of the stacking bet
4Where do Lightning sends get abandoned, by step?→ which Travel Rule fix comes first
5How many months do borrowers stack before their first loan?→ when the calculator should appear
6What share of borrowers were stackers first?→ whether the thesis holds
7How many spend events a month do retained users have, US and EU?→ whether spending is the retention lever
8What share of EU depositors make a second deposit?→ whether activation turns into a habit
9What does your bank charge for a Direct Debit, and for one that comes back?→ whether a weekly Direct Debit pays for itself
10How much of the 0.22% spread does Strike keep, and what would Apple Pay cost?→ whether to charge for Apple Pay or carry it
11What share of business accounts are one-person companies?→ how big the business-to-personal move is
Calls only you can make
  • Apple Pay: charge it or carry it
  • A card: which model, if any
  • Weekly deposits: free recurring buy or auto-buy
  • A paid tier next to free recurring buys
  • The E0 split: 80/20 or 50/50
  • A salary-capable EU IBAN
